name: cc-index-table
what_it_holds: Official tooling to build/query the Common Crawl columnar (Parquet/ORC) URL index. Includes CCIndex2Table, CCIndexExport, CCIndexWarcExport (Java), Docker support, and example SQL for AWS Athena / SparkSQL / Hive covering domain, language, MIME-type and content queries across the full crawl archive (not just one host). Apache-2.0.
why_useful: Lets us re-run the airbnb.com CDX capture at much larger scale/lower cost via serverless Athena SQL instead of the raw CDX API, and could be pointed at competitor domains (booking.com, vrbo.com, expedia.com, vacasa.com) to build comparable historical URL-presence panels for gap 9 (competitor supply) cheaply.
size_hint: tool; underlying columnar index is multi-TB on S3 (public, requester-pays for compute only)
themes: Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites
why_all: Lets us re-run the airbnb.com CDX capture at much larger scale/lower cost via serverless Athena SQL instead of the raw CDX API, and could be pointed at competitor domains (booking.com, vrbo.com, expedia.com, vacasa.com) to build comparable historical URL-presence panels for gap 9 (competitor supply) cheaply.

name: cc-pyspark
what_it_holds: Example PySpark jobs to process CC WARC/WAT/WET at scale: HTML tag frequency, server identification, IP extraction, word/doc frequency, link extraction and web-graph construction, plus SQL querying of the columnar index. MIT license, 157 commits, Python 3.9+/Spark 3.2+.
why_useful: Base framework for any large-scale reprocessing of Common Crawl WARC data touching travel sites (e.g., extracting hotel/listing counts, price mentions, or link graphs to competitor sites) beyond the single-host capture we already have.
themes: Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites
why_all: Base framework for any large-scale reprocessing of Common Crawl WARC data touching travel sites (e.g., extracting hotel/listing counts, price mentions, or link graphs to competitor sites) beyond the single-host capture we already have.

name: sodapy
what_it_holds: The canonical Python client for the Socrata Open Data API (430 stars, MIT, updated Aug 2026). No data of its own, but is the standard method for pulling any Socrata-hosted portal programmatically — this is the underlying transport for NYC Open Data, LA GeoHub/data.lacity.org, Austin's open data portal, Chicago data portal, SF DataSF, Seattle, and many state portals, most of which carry STR registration/licence datasets.
why_useful: Directly the tool named in CONTEXT.md gap 17 ("Socrata/CKAN open-data discovery clients to find STR datasets across cities"). Enables systematic re-pulls / longer-history queries against the municipal STR registries the team already holds (Austin, NYC OSE, etc.) and could reach additional Socrata cities not yet scraped.
duplicate_of_holding: we already hold Austin/Barcelona/Maui/NYC OSE/California TOT STR registries; sodapy is the acquisition method that could extend or refresh those, not new data itself
themes: Open-data portal discovery: Socrata/CKAN/data.gov/EU data portal clients, dataset search tools, Google Dataset Search scrapers; city portals with STR datasets
why_all: Directly the tool named in CONTEXT.md gap 17 ("Socrata/CKAN open-data discovery clients to find STR datasets across cities"). Enables systematic re-pulls / longer-history queries against the municipal STR registries the team already holds (Austin, NYC OSE, etc.) and could reach additional Socrata cities not yet scraped.

name: ceres-open-data-index (Ceres companion dataset)
what_it_holds: Parquet snapshot(s) of the Ceres harvester's normalized metadata index across 300+ open-data portals (see Ceres repo above); hosted on Hugging Face, ~8.24MB, last updated ~26 days before 14 Sep 2026 (i.e. mid-Aug 2026).
why_useful: A ready-made, already-harvested index (no need to run the crawler) that can be filtered offline for dataset titles/tags matching STR, short-term rental, tourism, lodging-tax, or vacation-rental across many jurisdictions — a shortcut to gaps 8, 9, 12.

name: mcp-opendatasoft
what_it_holds: MCP server / generic client for the ~3,000 public OpenDataSoft portal instances (e.g. public.opendatasoft.com, data.paris.fr, data.economie.gouv.fr). Tools for dataset search, metadata retrieval, SQL-style record queries, and facet exploration. MIT license, small (6 commits).
why_useful: OpenDataSoft powers many European city and tourism-board portals; a generic query client makes it tractable to pull STR/tourism datasets from EU cities named in gaps 7 and 12 (Amsterdam, Berlin, Vienna, Lisbon, France) without hand-building per-city API calls.
